summary: This is the Python SDK for runtimes 494 and 495. Release 494 published no Python packages, so this is the first SDK release with its features: channel commitments with optional burns (SetChannelCommitment, SetCommitBurn, and btcli commitments), weight delegation for one mechanism (SetMechWeightDelegate, the for_hotkey option of the weight intents, and btcli weights delegate), and the commit_burn, channel_commitment, and mech_weight_delegate reads. The channel_commitment read and btcli commitments show decode a commitment that the node returns as text (the read failed with ValueError before) and keep revealed text that starts with 0x as it is (#3359). For runtime 495, SetWeights and CommitWeights check the Null weight-row cap of 2500 divided by the mechanism count before they sign or encrypt a row, and they apply the effective minimum row length. The check before a single-validator root claim follows the connected runtime: 130 claim units before runtime 495, then 258 units that also count queued dividend credits on subnets the fund does not hold. The subnet emission weights read and intent now take the owner rate limit from the chain, 360 blocks by default since runtime 494, not a fixed 50400 blocks. Help texts describe the Null capacity of 2500 UIDs for any mechanism count and the mechanism limits. The bittensor-core package has the same code as its previous release; only its version is new. Upgrade before you use these features on runtime 494 or 495.
